stress_failure_mode: Non-photochemical quenching (NPQ): photoprotective thermal dissipation reduces effective energy transfer under excess light; high-light stress decreases Fv/Fm and NPQ activation
stress_metric: NPQ coefficient (qN): 0 to 1 scale; Fv/Fm depression below 0.83
notes: Phase 0 is the gate for the entire system. Absorptance ~0.85 sets the upper bound on all downstream processes. Under shade adaptation antenna size increases; under high light NPQ activated to protect PSII.

carbon_fixation_rate: Supplies electrons for all carbon fixation
o2_evolution_rate: 28 µmol O2 m-2 s-1 at saturation
sequestration_potential: Proportional to net GPP (O2 = CO2 on molar basis)
stress_failure_mode: PSII photoinhibition: D1 protein oxidative damage under excess light; Mn4CaO5 cluster disruption under Mn deficiency; donor-side inhibition by Ca2+ or Cl- depletion
stress_metric: Fv/Fm depression rate under high light (hours); D1 protein turnover rate (molecules per PSII per hour)
notes: O2 evolution is the most directly measurable ecological output of photosynthesis. Standard gas exchange and fluorescence measurements provide both O2 and quantum yield simultaneously.

ecological_output: Proton gradient for ATP; electron carrier reduction
output_unit: µmol e- m-2 s-1; mV pmf
biomass_contribution: Determines ATP and NADPH available for biomass synthesis
sequestration_potential: Determines energetic efficiency of carbon fixation
efficiency_metric: Linear electron flow rate; cytochrome b6f turnover
stress_failure_mode: State transitions: antenna rebalancing between PSII and PSI limits linear flow efficiency under fluctuating light; cytochrome b6f rate-limitation under cold temperatures (<10°C); cyclic vs linear electron flow balance
stress_metric: Fraction of cyclic electron flow (CEF/LEF ratio); pmf collapse under cold stress
notes: The electron transport chain is a well-measured intermediate. Its rate-limiting role (cytochrome b6f) makes it a primary target for understanding whole-chain carbon flux limitations.

biomass_contribution: NADPH feeds N assimilation and fatty acid synthesis beyond carbon fixation
sequestration_potential: Reductant for chloroplast biosynthesis contributes to overall plant biomass
stress_failure_mode: Acceptor-side limitation: NADP+ depletion when Calvin cycle slow (drought); PSI photoinhibition under fluctuating light (rare but permanent damage); ferredoxin:thioredoxin reductase failure affects dark enzyme regulation
stress_metric: PSI quantum yield Y(NA) and Y(ND) partitioning; PSI photoinhibition assay (P700 recovery kinetics)
notes: PSI is more resistant to photoinhibition than PSII under most conditions. Acceptor-side limitation (NADP+ depletion) is the most common ecological stress signal at this phase.

ecological_output: ATP production; energy currency for growth
carbon_fixation_rate: ATP drives carbon fixation in Calvin cycle
biomass_contribution: ATP fuels all biosynthetic processes linked to growth; direct driver of RuBP regeneration
sequestration_potential: ATP drives carboxylation efficiency; insufficient ATP increases photorespiratory carbon loss
stress_failure_mode: Drought: pmf dissipation via passive H+ leak increases as membranes dehydrate; cold stress reduces membrane fluidity and H+ conductance; salt stress reduces ΔpH component
stress_metric: CF0 conductance coefficient gH+ (pmf dissipation rate); ATP/NADPH ratio deviation from 1.28
notes: ATP synthase activity is tightly regulated and rarely the primary bottleneck under optimal conditions. Under drought or salt stress it becomes a significant limitation as pmf is destabilized.

ecological_output: Net CO2 assimilation; primary carbon sequestration
carbon_fixation_rate: 20 µmol CO2 m-2 s-1 (C3 25°C saturating light 380 ppm CO2)
biomass_contribution: Rubisco activity determines gross biomass carbon input
sequestration_potential: Net carbon sequestration per leaf area; annual yield linked directly to An
efficiency_metric: Net CO2 assimilation rate (An); Rubisco carboxylation rate (Vc)
efficiency_value: 25.0 µmol CO2 m-2 s-1 (gross Vc at saturation)
stress_failure_mode: Photorespiration: CO2 release ~25% of gross fixation at 25°C 21% O2; temperature sensitivity critical: Sc/o falls with T so photorespiration increases sharply above 30°C; drought-induced stomatal closure raises CO2/O2 ratio inside leaf and amplifies photorespiration; CO2 substrate limitation at low atmospheric CO2
stress_metric: Photorespiration rate (Rd + Rp); Rubisco activation state (%); stomatal conductance gs (mmol H2O m-2 s-1)
notes: Phase 5 is the key ecological bottleneck. Photorespiration under current atmosphere wastes ~25-30% of light energy captured at Phase 0-4. This is the primary reason C4 and CAM plants outperform C3 under warm dry conditions.

ecological_output: G3P synthesis; RuBP regeneration; carbon skeleton supply
carbon_fixation_rate: Consumes fixed carbon budget (3 ATP 2 NADPH per CO2)
o2_evolution_rate: Indirect (determines how much fixed CO2 becomes biomass)
biomass_contribution: G3P is the immediate precursor to all plant biomass compounds
sequestration_potential: G3P export to cytosol enables sucrose and export carbon; starch for storage
efficiency_metric: G3P yield per CO2 fixed; ATP/NADPH utilization efficiency
efficiency_value: 0.93 (fraction of 3-PGA that reaches G3P vs lost to photorespiratory bypass)
stress_failure_mode: Pi limitation: low cytosolic Pi traps G3P in chloroplast; inhibits Calvin cycle turnover (feedback inhibition of ADP-glucose pyrophosphorylase); cold-induced Pi limitation from reduced sucrose synthesis and export
stress_metric: Triose phosphate utilization (TPU) limitation flag; cytosolic Pi concentration; starch synthesis rate as overflow indicator
notes: TPU limitation (triose phosphate utilization limitation) is a distinct and measurable phase bottleneck. When sucrose synthesis is too slow to consume G3P the Calvin cycle backs up. Common under high CO2 or cold temperatures.

ecological_output: Sucrose and starch production; phloem loading; sink supply
carbon_fixation_rate: Enables all plant growth and ecosystem carbon flows
biomass_contribution: Export of sucrose to phloem fuels growth throughout the plant; starch remobilization sustains respiration overnight
sequestration_potential: Net ecosystem carbon balance depends on export vs respiration partitioning
efficiency_value: 0.75 (fraction of fixed carbon eventually exported to sinks)
stress_failure_mode: Sink limitation: when growth is slow (cold; nutrient stress) sucrose accumulates; feedback inhibition reduces An via starch accumulation and Pi trapping; phloem loading gene expression responds to temperature; night temperature determines starch remobilization rate
stress_metric: Starch/sucrose ratio at end of photoperiod; export efficiency (exported C / fixed C); NPP response to sink strength manipulations
notes: Phase 7 export regulation is partially opaque. In vivo phloem loading rates are difficult to measure non-invasively. Sink strength feedback on source photosynthesis is a major unresolved regulatory mechanism with large implications for crop yield.
